chunks: Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Jarood Ziyad ibn al-Munthir narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said:

When the Qa'im appears, he will appear with the banner of the Messenger of Allah, the ring of Solomon, and the rock and staff of Moses. Then he will order his caller to announce: 'Let no man among you carry food, drink, or fodder.' His companions will say: 'He intends to kill us and our cattle through hunger and thirst.' He will travel and they will travel with him, and at the first dwelling he reaches, he will strike a rock, from which food, drink, and fodder will gush forth. They will eat and drink, and their cattle [will feed], until they descend at Najaf on the outskirts of Kufa.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Awaited Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.رَايَةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The banner of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the signs and miraculous provisions associated with the appearance of al-Qa'im?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the eschatological authority of al-Qa'im by linking him to prophetic lineage through the possession of the Seal of Solomon and Moses' Staff, symbols of divine power and kingship. The miracle of the rock providing sustenance echoes the Quranic account of the Israelites, emphasizing that the Imam’s followers will be divinely sustained during their journey to Najaf near Kufa, a site of significant Shia historical and spiritual importance.
